surfaceContract.voiceDescription: Direct, modern, and emotionally exact. The article is not a sign encyclopedia; its job is to give the reader one memorable way to recognize the transit in real life. Interesting before comprehensive. Verbs and scenes over adjective triplets. Prefer a clear observation over a polished abstraction. A memorable phrase earns its place only when it makes literal sense on the first read.
surfaceContract.person: Current Sky describes shared weather. Sky-to-sky placement copy uses collective language: 'we', 'people' when people collectively are the actual subject, 'someone', or a concrete shared scene. Never use 'you', 'your', 'yours', 'yourself', or 'yourselves'. Second person belongs to transit-to-natal copy. Historical owner-approved second-person originals are preserved in fixtures/sky-placement-historical-second-person.json and are excluded from active generation and judge calibration.

beats.requirement: 2-4 sentences. Sentence 1 is the standalone recognition quote: a complete line someone would remember or send to a friend. The reader promotes it into a bold callout and removes it from the article body. Begin with a lived premise, not a slogan or abstract placement summary. The remaining sentences form the meaning paragraph: explain what the planet governs and how the sign changes its method, pace, or priorities. Translate meaning into natural prose and behavior, never a keyword list. Name the transit only after the human situation is clear when possible.

What the planet-sign combination does in ordinary life. 2-4 sentences. Include the transit's pace (days, weeks, years, decades) somewhere in the article, usually here. Concrete evidence INVENTED FRESH for this placement - the kind of thing a reader would recognize from their own week. Build movement from pressure to choice to consequence. Do not line up three representative examples from work, family, relationships, or public life as if completing a coverage checklist; concrete nouns do not rescue a flat inventory. One charged sequence beats three interchangeable scenarios. (The spec's classic illustrations - unsent message, corrected coffee order, overfilled calendar - are teaching examples and BANNED in output; they leaked into every card of the first batch.) Explain the planet through behavior, never through a keyword list.

Name where the gift becomes the problem and end with a clean truth. 2-5 sentences. The shadow must be observable behavior, not an abstract warning. Name the exact cost: the delayed conversation, cancelled plan, overspending, overwork, one-sided agreement, or other source-supported consequence. A directive is allowed when it is specific. End on the strongest plain sentence; no dramatic metaphor, second aphorism, blessing, or soft summary after it.

surfaceContract.taglineRules: 2-5 words, imperative or sharp claim, no terminal period, no planet/sign name needed. In OUR voice, not CHANI's: plain everyday words, bite over sparkle.
surfaceContract.movesRules: 2-3 items. Each is one sentence, a specific doable action tied to THIS placement (CHANI model: 'emcee an open mic', not 'embrace the energy'). No generic coaching verbs (embrace, trust, align, manifest). A move that would work for any placement fails the swap test.
surfaceContract.loreBoundary: Sign lore, rulership, modality, elements-as-labels, symbols, and season history belong in an optional 'About [Sign]' block rendered separately, NEVER in the article body. The element may be felt in imagery (heat for Leo, depth for Scorpio) but never named as mechanics.

By slowing down your revolutionary impulses long enough to make them sustainable, you become the leader who doesn't just start movements, but help them last. Taurus & Taurus Rising This Uranus retrograde illuminates your 2nd house of self-worth and values before moving to your 1st house of identity.

positiveExamples.text: On May 18, Mercury squares Mars in your first house, bringing friction between your public life and your personal desires. You may feel pulled in two directions, one part of you wanting recognition and progress, the other part craving autonomy, space, or rest. This tension is not a sign that you’re failing. It’s a sign that something needs to be recalibrated. Let your actions come from clarity, not ego. The goal isn’t just to win. It’s to win in a way that doesn’t cost you your peace.

positiveExamples.text: You’ve built your life around being the one others can count on, steady, thoughtful, and in control. But this retrograde is asking you to face what you’ve been avoiding: the emotional cost of carrying other people’s baggage. Whether it was a betrayal, a power dynamic, or a debt that was never yours to begin with, you absorbed it to keep things moving. You may have pushed it down to stay functional, but your body remembers what your mind tried to forget. You’re not here to carry someone else’s pain just because you know how to survive it. Let yourself finally lay it down.
positiveExamples.author: Marie Satori

positiveExamples.text: Uranus stations direct in Taurus, waking us up to the changes we can no longer ignore. The New Moon in Aquarius demands a fresh start, one that pushes us past outdated limitations and toward radical reinvention. Meanwhile, Mars retrograde in Cancer keeps us emotionally tethered to old wounds and patterns, making it clear where we need to heal before we can fully move forward.

positiveExamples.text: Lilith in Libra lingers in your 10th house, casting a long shadow over your public life, your career, your reputation. Where have you let yourself be defined by expectations that were never yours to begin with? This lunation will make it clear: silence is a choice, and one that you cannot afford anymore. Mars in Cancer, forming a trine to this lunation, reminds you that not all battles require force. Some are fought with vulnerability, with the willingness to name what needs to be named. This is the power of releasing an old story so that a new one can begin.

article.hook: People can care deeply and still leave the rule untouched. Uranus in Pisces exposes the gap between feeling bad about suffering and changing what keeps producing it. The problem becomes harder to dismiss when three rejection letters use the same language and lead to the same dead end.
article.lived: Uranus spends roughly seven years in Pisces, long enough for separate complaints to expose a pattern. Someone spends months appealing the same denial and assumes the case is unusual. Then three families compare letters and find identical wording, identical delays, and identical reasons for rejection. The unanswered emails become evidence, and what was treated as private bad luck becomes a rule that can be named and challenged.
article.turn: Once the harm becomes visible, every case can start to feel urgent. The same person who collected the complaints starts answering every message, explaining every form, and missing sleep because the system still refuses to help. A campaign repeats the original harm when one exhausted person becomes the only way through it. Changing the rule requires a structure that survives after the first organizer needs rest.
moves: Compare three rejection letters before treating the problem as a private exception.
Put names, dates, and outcomes in one shared record so the proof does not live in one inbox.
Divide replies, meetings, and follow-up before the person who found the pattern becomes another unpaid system.
